Task: run an impeccable-style design pass on the secondary drawer panels of Email OS (Vue 3 desktop email client), then implement the fixes.

Context: a UI/UX review of the whole app scored this area 20/40 heuristics, attention 7/10. It was done from code only (nothing rendered), so treat findings as strong leads and verify them. Read PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md first (brand: focused, precise, trustworthy; keyboard-first; honest state; Seams-Only rule; anti-references: Gmail clutter, generic SaaS cards, optimistic UI). See .impeccable/critique/*.md for prior critique format. Main has just merged the reader/compose pass (PR #29, commits 114895e and 79d5486): read that diff (`git diff 720eac0 origin/main`) and REUSE the patterns it introduced (compact composer rows, one-line honest status, Seam underline on input rows, quoted/attachment rows) rather than inventing parallel ones. DraftsPanel embeds DraftEditorCore, which that PR already reworked; don't redo that, just make the panel fit around it.

Files in scope: src/components/DraftsPanel.vue, RemindersPanel.vue, ActivityPanel.vue, CachedTrashPanel.vue, how src/App.vue mounts them (grep `drawer ===`, around lines 2630-2700; the drawer header and panel h2 are duplicated), their CSS in src/assets/style.css (drafts ~1676-1810, drawers ~900-935, group detail ~2032), and tests (activity-panel, drafts.*, reminders.*, cached-trash).

Findings to verify and address, in priority order:
1. P1 Activity rows identify mail by raw conversationId / request ID and say "Retry with a new request ID" (ActivityPanel ~168, ~190, ~274). Show cached subject (or "Unknown conversation"), a FullDate in the trailing slot, a one-word status in sentence case with the colour on the status word (Amber/Coral/Ash); IDs go in a title attribute; button becomes "Retry". "Conversation groups"/"Show older groups" are jargon (e.g. "Bulk actions").
2. P1 Cached Trash (~205-217) has four stacked disclaimer paragraphs before data and bare button rows. Collapse to one Ash line ("Cached Trash only, not your full Gmail Trash." or similar, keep the coverage caveat in a title), use the compact row anatomy (sender Title, subject Body, date Label), keyboard row navigation, Refresh as ghost button, a real loading state.
3. P1 Drafts: .drafts-pane is a two-column grid inside a 460px drawer so the list is ~150px wide. Use one column where the editor replaces the list (with an easy back/Esc). Draft rows 36px: recipient Title, subject Body, date trailing; show revision only on conflict; fold the local-only note into one Ash line; remove the raw "Reply source is fixed: <ids>" exposure.
4. P1 Reminders: lowercase tab names, run-on status line ("· pending · revision 3"), up to four full-width sentence-length buttons, raw conversationId in the picker, a typed RFC3339 time field. Add real tabs with counts, compact rows (subject, due time, one-word phase), preset times (Later today, Tomorrow, Next week) with the ISO field behind "Custom", long explanations in titles. It is fixture-only today, so keep the scope proportionate: fix structure, density, copy and presets, but don't invent new backend behaviour.
5. P2 Duplicate headings: App.vue drawer header and each panel's own h2 repeat the title; the aside nests in a role=region. Drop one (keep an accessible name).
6. P2 Row separators / bordered group-detail boxes (style.css ~1676-1681, ~1804-1813, ~2032): separate by rhythm, not borders, unless DESIGN.md explicitly allows them in drawers.
7. No keyboard model in any drawer: build one shared drawer-row pattern (roving tabindex, J/K or arrow keys, Enter to open, Esc to close/return), used by all four panels.
8. Spacing: the drawers use off-scale rem spacing (0.3/0.5/0.75/0.8rem) and ignore the 50px content inset. Align them with the documented scale and the list's inset; add tokens only if DESIGN.md needs them.

Constraints: honour PRODUCT.md "Standing constraints" and anti-references; honest state is the product (keep pending/partial/failed/unknown outcomes visible and distinct; never imply success that isn't confirmed; keep the evidence, move it from prose into titles/details rather than deleting it). Don't regress existing behaviour: explicit action labels, editable/IME shortcut protection, reduced-motion, announcements, focus handling, Undo/Retry semantics. Copy terse, sentence-case, factual. Do NOT touch the account/first-run surfaces (AccountPanel, ProviderDestinations, empty-inbox state), the bulk selection bar/notice dock, the reader/compose, or search; those are separate work. No real provider writes.

Process: first write a short critique of the area to .impeccable/critique/ in the existing format (verify the findings above against the code and tests; note any that turn out wrong). Then use the repo's `implement` skill / persona-feature-engineer agent to implement, update or add tests, run the project's checks (see mise.toml and docs/development.md; run pnpm install first if node_modules is missing), and update DESIGN.md if tokens or patterns change. Commit on this branch and open a PR to main. Report back with what changed, what you verified, what you could not verify (e.g. no rendered screenshots), and any findings you rejected.
I'll start by reading the product docs, prior critique format, and the merged reader/compose diff.

1	# Product
2	
3	## Register
4	
5	product
6	
7	## Users
8	
9	Initially a single person: the author, dogfooding a single-account desktop client (macOS first) against their own Gmail inbox in focused, keyboard-first sessions. They move through a high volume of mail quickly, want to reach "done" on each conversation, and need to trust that every action (archive, bulk processing, undo, send) did exactly what it claimed. The provider's own client remains the fallback.
10	
11	Longer term: technically capable people who want to compose their own email workflow (custom views, triage signals, commands, automations), manually or with an agent, without rebuilding sync, credentials, or send safety.
12	
13	The primary task on most screens is triage: scan the list, open a conversation, decide, act, move on.
14	
15	## Product Purpose
16	
17	A composable email client: a trusted mail engine (sync, safe rendering, credentials, action execution) with replaceable signals, views, commands, and workflows on top. It ships an opinionated reference experience, a compact Superhuman-style browsing and keyboard flow, rather than a blank toolkit.
18	
19	The near-term goal is a complete, trustworthy inbox-processing session. Strategic scope is set by `docs/adr/0001-single-account-desktop-email-client.md` and `superhuman-email-browsing-ux-spec.md`; this file does not expand it.
20	
21	Success looks like: the author processes their inbox faster and with more confidence than in their previous client, and every automated or bulk action is previewable, reported honestly (including partial success and "outcome unknown"), and undoable where undo is real.
22	
23	## Brand Personality
24	
25	**Focused, precise, trustworthy.**
26	
27	- **Focused:** the interface recedes so the mail and the next decision are what's on screen. Dense, quiet, few competing elements.
28	- **Precise:** exact states, exact counts, exact wording. No vague "something went wrong", no rounded-off truth about what happened.
29	- **Trustworthy:** the client never overstates what it did. Pending, failed, partial, and ambiguous outcomes are visible and distinct. Automation shows its work before it acts.
30	
31	Voice is terse and factual: short labels, plain verbs, no exclamation marks, no cheerleading.
32	
33	## Anti-references
34	
35	- **Gmail-web clutter:** toolbars of rarely-used icons, chrome competing with content, permanent competing panels.
36	- **"AI magic" email products:** AI destinations, sparkle icons, generated summaries presented as fact, fabricated contact enrichment, automation that acts without a preview.
37	- **Superhuman feature-parity clone:** Superhuman is the visual and interaction reference for browsing (layout, density, type, keyboard feel), and close look parity there is a goal. Features and workflows are our own; don't import Superhuman's product scope or claim verified behavioral parity.
38	- **Generic SaaS dashboard aesthetics:** card stacks and grids, gradient heroes, oversized rounded panels, decorative illustration or motion.
39	- **Optimistic UI that lies:** "Done" before the provider confirmed, silent retries of ambiguous sends, dead controls that look actionable.
40	
41	## Design Principles
42	
43	1. **Honest state over smooth feel.** When speed and truthfulness conflict, show the truth. Every action has a visible pending, success, partial, failed, or unknown state. Show evidence and coverage, including unknown and retained facts.
44	2. **Keyboard first, mouse welcome.** Every core triage path is reachable and discoverable from the keyboard; pointer interaction is supported, never required.
45	3. **Content is the interface.** Chrome stays quiet and compact so the list and the conversation dominate. Add UI only when it earns its space in the triage loop; reuse established commands, navigation and recovery surfaces before adding new ones.
46	4. **Preview before power.** Bulk actions, automations, and agent-proposed changes show what they will do before they do it, and report exactly what they did after. Focus, bulk selection and message identity stay separate concepts.
47	5. **Opinionated defaults, replaceable parts.** Ship one strong way of working; design surfaces so views, signals, and commands can be swapped without breaking the core experience.
48	
49	Standing constraints: ordinary reading stays local and non-mutating; message content renders as safe literal plain text; drafts stay local-only.
50	
51	## Accessibility & Inclusion
52	
53	Not a formal priority at this stage; no WCAG conformance target or certification is implied. Keyboard operability and visible focus remain required because they are core to the keyboard-first model. Don't regress behavior that already exists (explicit action labels, editable/IME shortcut protection, reduced-motion alternatives, selection/outcome announcements). The existing desktop/contact breakpoints remain authoritative; no new mobile UI. Revisit if the audience expands beyond the author.

# Critique run 1: reader + reply/compose

Method: single-agent, code-and-test verification only. Nothing was rendered (no Chrome on this VM, no screenshots), so every visual claim below is read from CSS and templates, not measured. The prior whole-app review scored this area 22/40 and ranked it next (attention 8/10). Each of its findings was re-checked against the code and tests; verdicts are marked CONFIRMED, PARTLY WRONG or REJECTED. Inbox list and search were critiqued earlier and are out of scope.

## Heuristics 23/40
| # | Heuristic | Score | Key issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Visibility of system status | 3 | "Saved locally / Saving locally…" exists but sits beside a 3-line disclaimer and is amber at rest |
| 2 | Match system / real world | 2 | Raw `conversationId · messageId` in the composer; "N bytes"; "Prepare reply" |
| 3 | User control and freedom | 3 | Esc flushes and closes, Discard confirms; no keyboard way to start a reply |
| 4 | Consistency and standards | 2 | Two reply glyphs; quoted block in mono while the body is proportional; reply form unlike every other reply UI |
| 5 | Error prevention | 3 | Fields disabled while a reply is unprepared; conflict and recovery paths are solid |
| 6 | Recognition rather than recall | 2 | No reply entry in the palette or key hints; the shortcut list says nothing about reply |
| 7 | Flexibility and efficiency | 2 | Reading is fully keyboard-driven (J/K/N/P/O/E/S/Z); replying is mouse-only |
| 8 | Aesthetic and minimalist design | 1 | Up to six caveat paragraphs above the thread; a 4-field form plus 3-line note plus ID line above 3 lines of typing room |
| 9 | Error recovery | 3 | Retry save, Save as new, Reload saved are explicit and honest |
| 10 | Help and documentation | 2 | A permanent disclaimer is doing the job a status line and a title should do |
| | **Total** | **23/40** | Acceptable |

Why 23 and not 22: `useDrafts.statusLabel` already yields an honest settled state ("Saved locally"), so the fix for the disclaimer is to promote that line, not invent a new one.

## Findings: verification

### 1. No reply shortcut — CONFIRMED, P1
`grep` finds no `r` binding anywhere in `App.vue`'s `onKeydown`, and `browsing-actions.ts` has no `reply` action. `prepareReply` (App.vue:1587) is reached only from `ReaderView` emitting `prepareReply`, from two controls: the header glyph `data-test="prepare-reply"` (ReaderView:710-720) and a per-message glyph on the active latest message (ReaderView:848-862). Reading is fully keyboard-driven (J/K/N/P/O/E/S/Z/C); replying is the one step that needs the pointer, which breaks "keyboard first" in the middle of the triage loop.
Safety already holds for a new key: the dispatcher returns for editable targets and IME (`isComposing`/`keyCode 229`, App.vue:1867-1869), returns early while a composer owns keys (App.vue:1866), and `actionShortcutBlocked` lets message toggles through but blocks other buttons. Reply must stay reader-only: the list holds no loaded message, so a list-level R would have to open, load and then reply, which is new scope. The source stays the displayed latest message (never the focused one), and the key must be unavailable for Cached Trash (`browsingOnly`), blocked replies (retained snapshot, incomplete, header mismatch), non-ready state and an open drawer.
Fix: add `reply` to `browsingActions` (label unchanged: "Prepare reply", shortcut R, so existing accessible names stay), `actionGroupOf`, `actionAliases` (respond, answer, write back), `actionAvailable`, `executeAction`, and the key handler; surface "R" in the header glyph title and palette; drive the reader's button titles from `actionLabel('reply')`.

### 2. Reply composer is a form — CONFIRMED, P1
`DraftEditorCore` renders four always-visible labelled fields (To, Cc, Subject, Body) in a 2-column grid (`.composer-fields`, style.css:1819), with a body that is `min-height: 8rem` (5rem when docked, style.css:2070). The core already pre-fills To and `Re: …` Subject for a reply (asserted in `reply-composer.component.test.ts:88-90`), so showing them as empty-looking boxes asks the user to re-read fields they never need to touch. Cc is optional and never filled for a reply. The new-message card needs To and Subject visible (they start empty) but Cc is rarely used.
Fix: reply surface gets a one-line recipient row ("To  Ada Fixture"), Cc and Subject behind a quiet "Cc / Subject" disclosure, and the body is the dominant, auto-focused field. New message keeps To and Subject visible and puts Cc on demand. The To row must never misrepresent the field: show the display name only while To is still the default sender mailbox, and the raw text once edited. Existing `data-test` hooks stay on the inputs; tests that read Cc or Subject reveal them first.
Quoted source: `.reply-quoted` is `--font-mono` at `--type-mono` (0.85rem), larger than the 12px shell and the proportional reading face above it (style.css, ReplyComposer.vue:154-165). Switch to the UI face at the body size in `--text-secondary` (4.99:1 on Focus Stone, ≥ 7:1 on `surface-raised`), keep the 2px rule and pre-wrap, keep it read-only and out of `bodyText`.

### 3. Permanent disclaimer and raw IDs — CONFIRMED, P1
`DraftEditorCore.vue:90-93` prints three lines on every open, every surface: "Local-only plain text. No Send action exists. Recipient text is stored raw… Cc is optional; Bcc, reply-all, quoted text, and rich text are not supported." It also contradicts the UI: it says quoted text is unsupported directly above a quoted block. `ReplyComposer.vue:110-112` and `DraftsPanel.vue:148` print `Reply source is fixed: <conversationId> · <messageId>`: opaque provider IDs a person cannot act on. The settled status line is `.draft-status`, which is colored `--warning` even when everything is fine, so amber at rest dilutes "local-only" as a real warning.
Fix: one line, "Saved locally · not sent" (settled, Ash) / "Saving locally…" / "Save not confirmed" (Amber Notice), with the detail ("Local plain-text draft. Nothing is sent. Recipients are stored as typed and not validated. Bcc, reply-all and rich text are not supported.") in the `title` and a visually hidden description for assistive tech. Drop the ID line from every surface; keep the IDs only as `data-source-*` attributes that tests can read (no visible text). The drawer's own `draft-local-note` in `DraftsPanel` stays (a different surface), but the editor core no longer duplicates it.
Footer: today it is `Close editor` / `Discard…` as equal ghosts with no key hint. Close already flushes (saves) first, and Esc does the same. Fix: primary "Save and close" (Esc kbd hint, Focus Stone fill, Title weight), secondary "Discard…" as an Ash ghost. Honesty is unchanged: the button still waits on the flush and the editor stays open with the error if it fails. No Send, ever.

### 4. Reader header caveats — CONFIRMED, P1
ReaderView:778-816 stacks up to six paragraphs under the subject before the first message: star line, reply-blocked, retained snapshot, one of three read-only/no-auto-read variants, unsupported-or-incomplete, pending. Two are standing statements repeated on every open: "Opening this conversation does not change read state; use an explicit read control" (Gmail with actions) and "Read-only Gmail view: messages are never marked as read. Opening this conversation does not change read state." (Gmail read-only), plus the Cached Trash text. The rest are real exceptions and should stay.
Fix: one muted status line in the existing meta row ("Unread" / "Read-only · Unread"), with the full sentence in its `title` and as visually hidden text, so the guarantee stays discoverable without repeating on screen. Keep every exception inline and amber: reply blocked, retained snapshot, unsupported/incomplete, pending, star attention. Keep the `reader-readonly` / `reader-no-auto-read` hooks on the status line. The Trash notice drops its "Opening does not change read state." sentence and keeps what Trash actually restricts.

### 5. Quoted blocks and signatures force monospace — CONFIRMED, P2
`bodyNeedsMonospace` returns true on the first line matching `^ {0,3}>`, so every reply-chain message renders entirely in mono (message-body-format.ts); two consecutive 4-space-indented lines (signatures, lists) do the same. The quoted tail is also what makes most real threads long.
Fix: split a plain-text body deterministically into prose, an optional signature (after a `-- ` delimiter, only when the tail is short) and an optional trailing quote (an "On … wrote:" attribution line, or a contiguous run of `>` lines to the end). Decide monospace from the prose part only, render signature and quote in the reading face in Ash, and put the quote behind a "Show quoted text" disclosure (per message, kept in the visit state so it survives J/K round trips). Still literal text via interpolation, the `>` characters are never rewritten, nothing is dropped, and interleaved (inline) quotes stay in place and keep the mono rule. The collapsed-row snippet uses the prose part so a message that is mostly quote does not preview as `>`.

### 6. Attachments are second-class — CONFIRMED, P2
`ReaderView` never references `Message.hasAttachment` (a known-true/false/unknown DTO field). Attachments are reachable only through the Cmd+O chooser (a modal). `AttachmentChooser.vue:91` prints `{{ file.size }} bytes` (a 4,812,333-byte file reads as a 7-digit number), and a 230-character paragraph sits above the list (lines 84-85). Its two lists share the same flat style.
Fix: inline attachment rows under the expanded body of each message that has files: name, human size ("27 B", "4.6 MB"), a Save button, and a Cancel while transferring, with the same pending/status/error semantics as the chooser (extract the save/cancel state into one shared composable, no second implementation). Where `hasAttachment === true` but no descriptor is cached, say so plainly ("Attachment not available offline: sync to fetch"); where it is unknown, show nothing (never inferred). Over-5-MiB files say "Over 5 MiB limit". The chooser keeps its role for links and the full list, loses the raw byte counts, and its intro paragraph shrinks to one line with the rest in a `title`/muted note ("Download only. Files save inert with a .download suffix.").

### 7. Loading state and type system — PARTLY WRONG
- Loading: the bare "Loading conversation…" shows only when the shell has no row identity (`loadingIdentity` null: Activity/Reminders/recent-mail entry). From the list the reader already shows the row's subject, sender and date first (ReaderView:735-742, tested). The holding state during J/K keeps the previous conversation on screen. Low value, P3. Small fix only: give the bare line `role="status"`; keep the exact text the smooth-navigation test pins.
- Collapsed sender column — REJECTED. `flex: 0 0 11em` at 12px is 132px, exactly the list's sender column. Its Ash/regular weight is deliberate: only the active message is Paper White/strong, which keeps the One Signal rule. Making it strong would erase that distinction.
- Uppercased date — REJECTED. `.message-time` uppercases the month exactly as `.row-time` does (style.css:1151 vs 1526), and DESIGN.md "Dates" specifies this ("6 Nov" in the DOM, "6 NOV" on screen). The reader already matches the list.
- Reply composer height — CONFIRMED. `.reply-composer { max-height: 45% }` with a 5rem textarea and a 4-field header, a 3-line note and an ID line leaves roughly three lines to type in, and the whole composer scrolls internally. The compact layout in findings 2 and 3 fixes this: the body gets a `min-height` of at least 6 lines and grows, the shell scrolls only when the thread and composer genuinely do not fit.

## Cross-cutting: contrast
Computed from the tokens (WCAG relative luminance): Graphite `#8e8a87` is 4.30:1 on Warm Charcoal, 3.79:1 on Lifted Charcoal `#33312e` and 2.75:1 on Focus Stone `#474644` (under the 3:1 non-text floor). Ash `#c0bcb6` is 7.79 / 6.86 / 4.99:1 on the same three. Smoke `#a09c9a` is 5.41 / 4.76 / 3.46:1. Nothing new in this area may use Graphite for a meaningful glyph or text on Focus Stone, and Graphite text on Lifted Charcoal (3.79:1) is below the 4.5:1 text floor. Current offenders in scope: the `.message-details summary` label ("Details", Graphite text on the active message's `surface-raised` fill, 3.79:1) and the `.message-reply` glyph on the same fill (passes 3:1 as a glyph, but text-sized hints do not). New composer glyphs and hints use Ash.

## Remaining priority issues (after this pass)
- P2 — The inline reply composer and the new-message card still scroll internally when the thread is very short. A true minimum thread viewport needs a rendered pass.
- P3 — The two reply glyphs (header and per-message) overlap in function; after R lands, the per-message glyph could go. Left in place: removing a visible control is a separate decision.
- P3 — Recipient autocompletion and validation do not exist by design (raw text, drafts local-only).

## Rendered check (added after implementation)
The fixture-only browser preview (Vite dev server, 1280×800, T3 browser) was driven through: open conversation → R → reply composer (body focused, `To  Ada Fixture`, status line, footer) → Cc / Subject → expand first message (inline attachment row, `27 B · text/plain`, Save) → Esc (focus back on the active message) → C (new-message card) → 20px root font. One defect only visible when rendered: empty Cc/To/Subject inputs had a transparent border, so the row looked like plain text; fixed with a Seam underline at rest. Seen but out of scope: the contact pane's "Composing to …" line pushes the contact name 33px off the tab line while a draft is open (ContactPane, untouched); closing the docked new-message card leaves focus on `<body>` (reply composer now restores it).
Not rendered: the quote toggle (no fixture message has a quote), Gmail-mode status line, Cached Trash, blocked-reply states; those are covered by component tests only.

## Not verified
Contrast numbers are computed from tokens, not sampled from pixels. Native/WKWebView is not exercised. Contrast numbers are computed from the tokens, not sampled from pixels. Real-Chrome journeys (`reader.rendered.test.ts`) are opt-in on `EMAIL_OS_RENDERED_LAYOUT_CHROME` and cannot run on this VM.

# Development guide

This repository contains two deliberately separate native profiles: the durable
synthetic fixture slice (Slice 01) and an explicit Gmail profile built in stages.
Slice 02 adds system-browser OAuth/PKCE, a macOS Keychain credential store,
bounded inbox caching, and background sync. Slice 03 adds opt-in, durable Gmail
archive/unarchive and explicit read/unread actions; Gmail remains read-only until
the user explicitly requests the broader Google `gmail.modify` permission.
Slice 04 adds a local-only plain-text composer and durable draft recovery, but
still does not send/delete mail or expose arbitrary labels. Opening a message
never marks it read. UX-05 adds bounded multi-select and durable bulk
archive/read group processing with one-level partial group Undo; the browser
preview remains synthetic and in-memory. See
the slice contracts for individual acceptance scope. UX-08 adds narrow Gmail-mode
Star/Unstar singles/groups, durable Undo/reconciliation, cache-only Starred and a
single cached starred filter; see [its contract and validation ledger](ux-08-stars.md).
The legacy native fixture remains archive-only; unsupported star controls are
absent there. No real provider writes are authorized by implementation tests.
UX-06 adds one durable local
sender/domain split over Inbox, exact cached-count badges, and a single unread
filter. See [the saved-split contract](ux-06-saved-split.md) for matching,
keyboard navigation, cache coverage, and persistence boundaries.

## Layout

| Path | Owner |
|---|---|
| `crates/mail-core/` | Rust DTOs, fixture core, Gmail provider/auth/cache/sync/actions, SQLite, profile locks |
| `src/`, `tests/`, `package.json`, configs | Vue 3/TypeScript frontend, IPC adapter and tests |
| `src/lib/ipc/generated.ts` | **Generated** — do not edit by hand; regenerate with `mise run gen:ts` |
| `src-tauri/` | Thin Tauri 2 shell: typed mail/draft/close commands, `mailbox_changed` and `drafts_changed` hints, fixture/Gmail profile selection and lifecycle |
| `mise.toml` | Project tasks (see below) |

## UX-09 increment A: read-only provider mail

The **Provider mail** rail entry (Gmail native or labelled browser preview) opens
a bounded destination browser for Sent, provider Drafts, All Mail, Spam, Trash
and user labels. Search covers the loaded catalog; Show more expands it. It is
not mailbox search. All Mail excludes Spam/Trash. Every page contains at most
25 conversations, at most 16 MiB of serialized thread DTOs, and no exact total.
The read-only drawer intentionally has no triage/reply controls. Its page remains
mounted during a reader visit; closing the drawer returns to the prior inbox
context. This is not yet the roadmap's integrated main-list destination context.

Native commands `list_provider_destinations(accountId, cached)` and
`browse_provider_destination(request)` run off the UI thread, require the active
account, and use readonly Gmail APIs. Page cursors carry account+destination
identity and a bounded opaque provider token; they grant no authority.
A separate SQLite table retains one catalog and up to 20 destination snapshots
(latest successful page per retained destination), independent of inbox discovery,
history and operation recovery. **Use saved catalog/page** is explicit and
timestamped; provider failures are never silently converted to saved success or
an empty list. Restart retains these snapshots; disconnect clears them.

Provider Drafts are read-only snapshots, **not** the app's local editable drafts.
The native fixture rejects both provider commands; browser preview models them
in memory only. Label/Move, label badges on ordinary inbox rows, palette integration,
and saved-view/search criteria are not implemented here. After rebasing onto
`b4972ee`, the UX-06/07/08 contracts are preserved but not extended by this

## How to design

- **The brief wins.** Honor pinned aesthetics, eras, materials, fonts, and palettes even when they conflict with a saturated-pattern warning. Redirecting a clear brief toward your taste is failure.
- **Refinement preserves; redesign replaces.** Refinement keeps the incumbent identity, behavior, copy, and everything outside scope. Ask before replacing factual copy or adding claims. Redesign keeps product truth, content, function, native affordances, and constraints, but treats the old look as evidence and anti-reference; choose a replacement world in new-work and replace DESIGN.md. Never split the difference into polish on the discarded look.
- **Loaded symbols stay out of the decoration.** A subject's world does not license emblems tied to militarism, supremacy, or hate movements as motifs, badges, or ornament, such as the Rising Sun flag's rays, the Confederate battle flag, or Nazi-era insignia and their stylised variants; reach for that world's neutral forms instead. Content that documents such a symbol as fact stays as it is.
- **Visual authority is evidence, not a filename.** Missing DESIGN.md alone does not make a project greenfield; new-work decides whether to preserve, expand, or replace the incumbent world.

## Modes

The mode names what the visitor's success looks like on this surface.

- **Persuade:** the visitor decides and acts; design is the product. Landing pages, marketing, campaigns, pricing. Earn attention and action. Ship real imagery when the brief needs it; follow the committed world, not category habit.
- **Operate:** the visitor completes a task. App UI, dashboards, editors, admin, settings, tools. Scanability, consistency, native expectations, and the real usage scene outrank expression. Brand lives in precise details.
- **Read:** the visitor understands something. Docs, articles, guides, help, changelogs. Structure for comprehension, then make the reading experience worth staying in.
- **Experience:** the visitor is inside the work itself. Portfolios, galleries, showcases. Let the artifact lead from the first viewport; the interface recedes.

# Product

## Register

product

## Users

Initially a single person: the author, dogfooding a single-account desktop client (macOS first) against their own Gmail inbox in focused, keyboard-first sessions. They move through a high volume of mail quickly, want to reach "done" on each conversation, and need to trust that every action (archive, bulk processing, undo, send) did exactly what it claimed. The provider's own client remains the fallback.

Longer term: technically capable people who want to compose their own email workflow (custom views, triage signals, commands, automations), manually or with an agent, without rebuilding sync, credentials, or send safety.

The primary task on most screens is triage: scan the list, open a conversation, decide, act, move on.

## Product Purpose

A composable email client: a trusted mail engine (sync, safe rendering, credentials, action execution) with replaceable signals, views, commands, and workflows on top. It ships an opinionated reference experience, a compact Superhuman-style browsing and keyboard flow, rather than a blank toolkit.

The near-term goal is a complete, trustworthy inbox-processing session. Strategic scope is set by `docs/adr/0001-single-account-desktop-email-client.md` and `superhuman-email-browsing-ux-spec.md`; this file does not expand it.

Success looks like: the author processes their inbox faster and with more confidence than in their previous client, and every automated or bulk action is previewable, reported honestly (including partial success and "outcome unknown"), and undoable where undo is real.

## Brand Personality

**Focused, precise, trustworthy.**

- **Focused:** the interface recedes so the mail and the next decision are what's on screen. Dense, quiet, few competing elements.
- **Precise:** exact states, exact counts, exact wording. No vague "something went wrong", no rounded-off truth about what happened.
- **Trustworthy:** the client never overstates what it did. Pending, failed, partial, and ambiguous outcomes are visible and distinct. Automation shows its work before it acts.

Voice is terse and factual: short labels, plain verbs, no exclamation marks, no cheerleading.

## Anti-references

- **Gmail-web clutter:** toolbars of rarely-used icons, chrome competing with content, permanent competing panels.
- **"AI magic" email products:** AI destinations, sparkle icons, generated summaries presented as fact, fabricated contact enrichment, automation that acts without a preview.
- **Superhuman feature-parity clone:** Superhuman is the visual and interaction reference for browsing (layout, density, type, keyboard feel), and close look parity there is a goal. Features and workflows are our own; don't import Superhuman's product scope or claim verified behavioral parity.
- **Generic SaaS dashboard aesthetics:** card stacks and grids, gradient heroes, oversized rounded panels, decorative illustration or motion.

## Verify

Each of these is a check on the built result, not an intention. Run them together in each batched look at the render, not as separate screenshot trips; the checks share one render.

- **Contrast:** body and placeholder text ≥4.5:1, large text ≥3:1. On colored surfaces tint secondary text from that hue or the foreground; never gray.
- **Depth:** shadows carry an offset and a soft blur. A zero-offset colored halo is decoration.
- **Spacing:** tight groups, generous separation, more space above a heading than below it. Read the computed values.
- **Type:** body measure 65–75ch, display max 6rem, tracking floor -0.04em, balanced headings, obvious scale and weight steps. Run the real copy at every breakpoint and fix what overflows.
- **Motion:** one authored moment, not scattered effects and not one identical entrance on every section. Exponential ease-out from an already-visible default. Reach past transform and opacity: blur, backdrop-filter, clip-path, mask, and shadow belong to the palette when they stay smooth.
- **States:** hover, disabled, loading, error, empty. Plus real content, working controls, responsive composition, keyboard focus.
- **Browser surfaces:** the parts you did not draw still carry the design. These are the category's defaults, not bans: the brief's own words can earn any of them. Reaching for one when the axis is free means you were not deciding; recognizing that means rewriting the element, not softening it.

Page scaffolds:

- Same-size cards of icon plus heading plus text as the page structure. Cards are the lazy container; nested cards are always wrong.

- A kicker or eyebrow above a heading. This one is a ban, not a default: no brief earns it back. The heading carries its own weight; delete the label and let the heading speak.

- Gradient text. Emphasis comes from weight or size.

A view belongs in the main pane when its rows are conversations the user triages, opens and returns to. It stays a drawer when it is a log or settings glanced at without leaving one's place. 1. **Cached Trash becomes a read-only list context (P1).** Already a read-only list of `ConversationSummary` rows; the drawer duplicates the list's row anatomy in a 460px column and is the only list needing special origin handling (`captureListOrigin('trash')`, `trashReader`, re-opening the drawer on Back, ActionNotice suppression `drawer !== 'trash'`). Needs a read-only list mode: no row actions, no selection, no mailbox shortcuts (the existing tests pin that no `setArchived` / `setRead` / group call happens and no reply control shows).
2. **Reminders becomes a list context (P1).** A pending reminder removes the conversation from Inbox until it is due, so it is a place mail lives (`docs/ux-11-local-reminders.md` calls it a "standalone pending/returned destination"). Pending / Returned / History are views of that list; Reschedule and Cancel are row actions; the time picker is an in-flow block, not a modal. Fixture-only stays fixture-only (`remindersSupported`); no new rail slot (the header glyph and `G H` remain the entries); no new backend behaviour.
3. **Drafts becomes a main-pane list; opening a draft navigates to its source (P1).** Decided by the owner: a reply draft opens the source conversation's reader with the docked reply composer (the existing reply flow); a new-message draft opens the existing inline compose card.
